item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q014_paper_example_reclassification_pa1492","answer":"In SCOP 1.69, PA1492 (1t1j; representative main domain d1t1ja_) was c.137.1.1: its own PA1492 fold c.137 and superfamily c.137.1. Nucleoside 2-deoxyribosyltransferase (1f8y; d1f8ya_) was c.23.14.1: the flavodoxin-like fold c.23 and N-deoxyribosyltransferase superfamily c.23.14. They therefore shared only the broad alpha/beta class c; SCOP asserted no closer relationship. In the current SCOPe release 2.08, PA1492’s main domain d1t1ja1 (residues 1–118) is reclassified as c.23.14.2. It now shares the flavodoxin-like fold c.23 and N-(deoxy)ribosyltransferase-like superfamily c.23.14 with 1f8y, supporting probable common ancestry, while remaining in a separate PA1492 family (.2 versus the enzyme’s .1). Both biological chains give the same conclusion; the additional l.1.1.1 zero-residue/tag records for 1t1j are not the PA1492 structural domain. Superfamily membership does not establish that PA1492 has nucleoside 2-deoxyribosyltransferase activity or justify transferring active-site details without independent sequence, structural-site, or biochemical evidence; it supports only cautious homologous-template use.","evidence_used":["mcp__scope__get_scop_service_info — /api/v1/, /api/v1/releases/current","mcp__scope__get_scop_pdb_entry — /api/v1/releases/1.69/pdb/1t1j/domains, /api/v1/releases/1.69/pdb/1f8y/domains, /api/v1/releases/2.08/pdb/1t1j/domains, /api/v1/releases/2.08/pdb/1f8y/domains","mcp__scope__get_scop_domains — /api/v1/releases/1.69/sids/d1t1ja_, /api/v1/releases/1.69/sids/d1t1ja_/parents, /api/v1/releases/1.69/sids/d1f8ya_, /api/v1/releases/1.69/sids/d1f8ya_/parents, /api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1t1ja1, /api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1t1ja1/parents, /api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1f8ya_, /api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1f8ya_/parents","mcp__scope__compare_scop_domains — the corresponding 1.69 and 2.08 SID, /parents, and /homology paths listed above"]}]}
